events.name: Committee to find a lot for the African Church (Richard Allen, Absalom Jones, William Gray, William Wilcher)
events.location: Philadelphia: lot at Lombard and Sixth streets, then a lot in Fifth street
events.description: Richard Allen's own account. After the Methodist elder threatened to disown them, Allen and the Rev. Absalom Jones went out with a subscription paper for an African church and collected three hundred and sixty dollars the first day. "We appointed a committee to look out for a lot—the Rev. Absalom Jones, William Gray, William Wilcher and myself. We pitched upon a lot at the corner of Lombard and Sixth streets." Allen agreed for that lot with Mr. Mark Wilcox. The committee then bought a lot in Fifth street instead and left the first lot on Allen's hands; he kept it, and it became the site of Bethel. Allen "put the first spade in the ground to dig a cellar" for the African church, "the first African church or meeting-house that was erected in the United States of America." The members voted to unite with the Church of England, with only Allen and Jones voting Methodist. This African Church is the later St. Thomas African Episcopal Church; Allen does not use that name. || Source: Richard Allen, The Life, Experience, and Gospel Labors of the Rt. Rev. Richard Allen (Philadelphia, 1880), pp. 17-18. The book gives no date for the committee. The year 1793 is printed on p. 19, where a committee from the African Church asks Allen to be its minister.
